title: 異文化理解・コミュニケーション
subtitle: Intercultural Understanding and Communication
teachers:
KANO Tsuyoshi
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: This course is designed to achieve the educational goal of the Department of Environmental Design Creation: “fundamental abilities for collaborative work through communication.” Communication in a global society refers not only to language skills but also to the ability to build trust by understanding the cultures and values of others. This course aims to cultivate individuals who can transform potential cultural and value differences in a global society into mutual understanding rather than friction.
advice: This course explores various forms of cross-cultural understanding and communication based on business administration and international affairs, addressing questions such as “What is a global society?” and “What constitutes a different culture?” (This is not a foreign language course like English). Subsequently, it aims to impart knowledge and practice communication patterns in business situations based on cultural differences between countries. This focuses on the communication skills necessary to effectively utilize an organization as a member of a global team, with the goal of mastering these techniques. Furthermore, students will examine how to effectively utilize their communication skills within the organizations they are involved in and share these insights with other participants.
requiredKnowledge: Different cultures exist in every aspect of daily life. While this is especially true in environments where people come from different countries, even individuals of the same nationality inevitably have differences in their ways of thinking and values based on the regions and environments where they grew up. It is desirable to maintain an interest and awareness of what is happening in the world and in Japan today through the daily habit of reading newspapers and watching the news.

              This course is designed to achieve the educational goal of the Department of Environmental Design Creation: “fundamental abilities for collaborative work through communication.” Communication in a global society refers not only to language skills but also to the ability to build trust by understanding the cultures and values of others. This course aims to cultivate individuals who can transform potential cultural and value differences in a global society into mutual understanding rather than friction.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course explores various forms of cross-cultural understanding and communication based on business administration and international affairs, addressing questions such as “What is a global society?” and “What constitutes a different culture?” (This is not a foreign language course like English). Subsequently, it aims to impart knowledge and practice communication patterns in business situations based on cultural differences between countries. This focuses on the communication skills necessary to effectively utilize an organization as a member of a global team, with the goal of mastering these techniques. Furthermore, students will examine how to effectively utilize their communication skills within the organizations they are involved in and share these insights with other participants.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Culture Map, Erin Maylor

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              Different cultures exist in every aspect of daily life. While this is especially true in environments where people come from different countries, even individuals of the same nationality inevitably have differences in their ways of thinking and values based on the regions and environments where they grew up. It is desirable to maintain an interest and awareness of what is happening in the world and in Japan today through the daily habit of reading newspapers and watching the news.
